title: Best Signage Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a signage designer for shops, offices and events: what to include, production files, readability, price factors and red flags.
intro: Signs guide people, attract customers and show your brand on shopfronts, windows, walls, banners and events. Good signage is readable from the right distance and produced correctly by the sign maker. It goes wrong when files do not match production requirements, text is too small for the viewing distance, or local rules on signs are ignored. This guide helps you order signs that work in the real world.

faq.q: What files does a sign maker need?
faq.a: Usually vector files at the exact size, with specified colors and any cut lines. Ask your sign maker for their requirements and share them with the designer.

faq.q: How large should the text be?
faq.a: It depends on viewing distance. Signs read from across a street need much larger text than signs read at a counter. Tell the designer where people will be when they read it.

faq.q: Do I need permission for outdoor signs?
faq.a: Often. Many places have rules for outdoor signs, including size, lighting and placement. Check with your landlord and local authority before production.

faq.q: Can the designer create a set of signs?
faq.a: Yes. Shop signs, window graphics, opening hours, wayfinding and event banners can share a consistent style.
Ask for one showing the sign on a photo of your location. It helps you judge size and colors.
